node.label: Reinhart Koselleck
node.date_label: Kritik und Krise (1959) · Preussen zwischen Reform und Revolution (1967) · Geschichtliche Grundbegriffe: first volume, coedited with Brunner and Conze (1972) · Vergangene Zukunft: original collection (1979) · Futures Past: Keith Tribe’s English translation (1985) · A Response to Comments on the Geschichtliche Grundbegriffe (1996) · Zeitschichten (2000) · Malin Dahlstrom reviews Olsen’s History in the Plural (2012)
node.description: A historian of political and social concepts and of historical time. He distinguishes words from concepts, the language of sources from analytical categories, and semantic change from direct reduction to social structures. He coedited the Geschichtliche Grundbegriffe with Otto Brunner and Werner Conze; collective authorship is retained. In Futures Past he examines the relation between experience and expectation, and in his published 1996 response he argues that the unique context of a speech act does not exclude tracing later reuse and transformation of concepts. His reply to Pocock defends the interdependence of conceptual and discourse history. Later accounts of his early books and temporal layers are explicitly mediated through Malin Dahlstrom’s review of Niklas Olsen.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Kritik und Krise (1959); Preussen zwischen Reform und Revolution (1967); with Otto Brunner and Werner Conze, Geschichtliche Grundbegriffe (first volume 1972, collective series); Vergangene Zukunft (1979; Keith Tribe’s English Futures Past, 1985; Columbia reissue 2004); “A Response to Comments on the Geschichtliche Grundbegriffe” (1996); Zeitschichten (2000). The 1959, 1967 and 2000 books are known here through Dahlstrom’s account of Olsen, not direct book-body readings.
node.scope_note: The retained Futures Past source records the exact earlier selected chapter/preface readings and their limits. Fresh 2026-10-24 reading: chapter 5 pp. 85 and 91–92, with the surrounding analytical distinctions; the 1996 reply pp. 59–66 closely, plus its concluding context; the complete six-page Dahlstrom review of Olsen. Original German texts, lexicon articles and the full 1959/1967/2000 books were not read. The lexicon’s 1972 date is bibliographic metadata; its methodological account rests separately on the primary reply and existing primary passages. Nietzsche’s quotation and Weber’s typology are specific resources, not total genealogies. New prose paraphrases rather than reproduces source quotations. The early-book reception is a reader’s report of another reader, with no new direct claim about Habermas’s uncollated review.

proposed_edges.relationship: Develops conceptual history through the collective lexicon and distinguishes a concept’s contextual uses from the history of its subsequent transmission and transformation (1972 project; published response 1996).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: The first volume’s date and joint credit are metadata; Koselleck’s 1996 pp. 59–66 and the existing Futures Past selected reading supply the methodological account. This contribution does not give him sole authorship of every lexicon entry. The Nietzsche and Weber resource arrows and his specific contribution to intellectual history retain their IDs with repaired individual endpoints.

proposed_edges.relationship: Answers Pocock’s objections by treating discourse and conceptual history as interdependent and defending alphabetical organization as a way to leave historical transformation open to investigation (published 1996).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Koselleck’s own response pp. 62–66, especially pp. 64–66, read. He accepts the uniqueness of situated speech acts but argues that later reception and reuse make conceptual history necessary. He rejects a general incompatibility of methods; this does not mean that Pocock himself asserted such a simple opposition. This is a qualified methodological answer to specific questions, not a complete rebuttal of Pocock’s scholarship.

verification.note: Complete six-page official Reviews in History PDF read in the web rendering: https://reviews.history.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/pdf/Reviews_in_History_-_History_in_the_Plural_An_Introduction_to_the_Work_of_Reinhart_Koselleck_-_2012_06_28.pdf . This is Dahlstrom’s account of Olsen’s account of Koselleck; Olsen’s full book and the books discussed remain unread in this pass. Supports qualified bibliography/dates for Kritik und Krise (1959), Preussen zwischen Reform und Revolution (1967) and Zeitschichten (2000), and attributed account of their arguments/reception. The 1953 dissertation date is not adopted because other existing bibliography dates the revised thesis 1954. The lexicon’s substantive completion and later index volumes are not conflated. No fresh quotation.

edges_considered_not_proposed: Do not create an unmediated Habermas-to-Koselleck critique from Dahlstrom’s report of Olsen.
Do not infer a full Weber genealogy from the single typological example.
No automatic equivalence between Cambridge contextualism and Begriffsgeschichte.
